title: Frames under sequential composition
statement: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be machines with the same input alphabet and number of work tapes, with state sets $S_1$ and $S_2$, and suppose $S_1$ has decidable equality. Let $C_1$ be a contract for $M_1$ from entry state $e_1$ to the singleton exit state $e_1'$, and let $C_2$ be a contract for $M_2$ from entry state $e_2$ to an exit set $X_2$. Let $\mathrm{link}$ map the data for $C_1$ to data for $C_2$, and suppose that whenever a starting configuration is in state $e_1$ and satisfies the precondition of $C_1$, the endpoint of $C_1$ with its state reset to $e_2$ satisfies the corresponding precondition of $C_2$. If $C_1$ and $C_2$ have the frame property for frame sets $fp_1$ and $fp_2$, respectively, then their sequentially composed contract has the frame property for the union of $fp_1$ at the starting configuration and $fp_2$ at the linked data and state-reset endpoint of $C_1$.
hypotheses_covered: M₁ and M₂ have the same input alphabet and number of work tapes
S₁ and S₂ are their state sets
C₁ is a contract for M₁ from e₁ to {e₁'}
C₂ is a contract for M₂ from e₂ to X₂
both contracts use the same fixed input
link maps C₁ data to C₂ data
each eligible C₁ endpoint, with its state reset to e₂, satisfies the corresponding C₂ precondition
C₁ has the frame property for fp₁
C₂ has the frame property for fp₂

state $e_2$ to an exit set $X_2$, both on the same input and with the same $k$ work
tapes. Suppose a map $\mathrm{link}$ sends each parameter of $C_1$ to a parameter of
$C_2$, and whenever a configuration satisfies the entry-state and precondition
hypotheses of $C_1$, the state-renamed endpoint of $C_1$ satisfies the corresponding

respective frame sets, then their sequentially composed contract preserves the work-tape
